clue.text: Finch is about to hide

indicators.note: about signals turning round the little word just before it, so is reads backwards

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin

explanation.surface: A small bird is on the point of going into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a verb going with 'about to', but it is a noun, an animal's skin; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green songbird of the finch family.

clue.text: Sentimental person frequently seen in Sleepy Hollow?

indicators.note: seen in places the adverb inside the emptied word
a hollow thing has nothing in the middle, so only the outer letters of Sleepy remain

parts.note: oft is an old word for frequently

explanation.surface: A soft-hearted character often found in the village of the Headless Horseman story.
explanation.walkthrough: Sleepy Hollow reads as the Washington Irving setting, but Hollow empties Sleepy to SY.
explanation.definitionFit: A softy is a soft-hearted, easily moved person, a sentimental type.

clue.text: A fly gets on top, going up and down

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top places the verb's letters above the rest

parts.note: to get something is to understand it, to see it
to fly is to wing one's way

explanation.surface: An insect lands on the uppermost point and bobs about.
explanation.definitionFit: Seesawing describes moving alternately up and down, like a playground plank.

clue.text: Devil's advocate comprehends woman in Casablanca

indicators.note: comprehends in its sense of includes: the phrase holds the name within its letters

explanation.surface: Someone arguing the contrary side understands a female character from the film.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the apostrophe: the run runs across devIL'S Advocate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilsa Lund, played by Ingrid Bergman, is the heroine of the film Casablanca.

clue.text: Expert given drink bursts into laughter

parts.note: crack as an adjective means expert, first-rate (a crack shot)
to sup is to drink, especially in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: A skilled person handed a glass starts roaring with laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack up is an informal idiom for collapsing into helpless laughter.

clue.text: Agent needs additional pay for further performance

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
a rise is an increase in wages in British usage

explanation.surface: A theatrical agent demands more money for an extra show.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprise is a repeated performance of a piece or a return to an earlier role.

clue.text: Convincing a dubious vice-consul

indicators.note: dubious means doubtful or shady, a sign that the official's letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A shady diplomat is persuasive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link; only the ten letters of vice-consul are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Conclusive evidence settles the matter, so it is convincing beyond doubt.

clue.text: Generate power that's cut out

indicators.note: out here works as outside: the cut word goes round the letter for power

parts.note: sawn means cut with a saw
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: To produce electricity which has been switched off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link; 'cut out' reads as an electrical failure, but SAWN placed outside P is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: To spawn is to produce or give rise to something, as fish produce eggs.

clue.text: One in temple possibly reformed stepsister wasting time

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the remaining letters are rearranged
wasting means losing, so one letter goes from the relative

explanation.surface: A reformed stepsister who fritters away the hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting time' takes one T out of STEPSISTER, leaving SEPSISTER to be rearranged; 'possibly' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A priestess serves a god in a temple, one example of someone found there.

clue.text: Keep forgetting names for cocktail

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving out, so letters are dropped from the verb

parts.note: to maintain is to keep something up
N is the abbreviation for name, so names gives two of them

explanation.surface: Repeatedly failing to recall what people are called, and ordering a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ns go from MAINTAIN, leaving MAITAI.
explanation.definitionFit: A mai tai is a rum-based cocktail with lime and orange flavours.

clue.text: Flower from independent kingdom formerly miles away

parts.note: free means independent, not under another's control

indicators.note: away means gone, so one letter leaves the old country name

parts.note: Siam is the former name of the kingdom of Thailand

explanation.surface: A bloom from a once-free realm grown far off.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant flowering plant from southern Africa, popular in bouquets.

clue.text: Asian shot in front of Princeton University

indicators.note: front of gives the opening letter of the place name
in places the injection inside the college word

parts.note: a jab is a shot, an injection

explanation.surface: Someone from Asia is shot outside a famous American college.
explanation.walkthrough: Princeton University looks like one name, but it splits in two: the front of Princeton, then the short word for a university with the shot inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Punjabi is a native of the Punjab region of India and Pakistan, so an Asian.

clue.text: In odd places you earn money abroad

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: Working overseas you get paid in unusual locations.
explanation.definitionFit: The yuan is the currency of China, a foreign unit of money.

clue.text: Youngsters doing multiplication in evacuated schools?

indicators.note: in places the arithmetic word inside the emptied word
evacuated means emptied, so only the outer letters of schools stay

parts.note: tripling is multiplying by three

explanation.surface: Children doing times tables in schools whose pupils were sent away.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripling is a youth, a young man not yet fully grown.

clue.text: Scrambling into a garment without finesse

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the garment goes round the rearranged word

parts.note: a dress is a garment

indicators.note: scrambling means mixing up, so the four letters of into are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clumsily wriggling into an outfit with no grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but here it has its old sense of outside, with 'Scrambling' rearranging the word into.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroitness is skill and deftness in handling things, much the same as finesse.

clue.text: Innocent Democrat taken in by cool president

indicators.note: taken in by puts the party letter inside the cold word

parts.note: to chill is to cool
D is the abbreviation for a US Democrat
Ike was the nickname of US president Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A naive Democrat is fooled by a laid-back head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Childlike means having a child's innocence and simplicity.

clue.text: Heading for Cambridge with light blue stopper?

indicators.note: heading for gives the first letter of the university town

parts.note: a lamp is a light
down and blue both mean sad, low in spirits

explanation.surface: A Cambridge rower in light blue colours setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: Light blue is Cambridge University's colour, which hides LAMP and DOWN. The question mark admits that a crackdown is only loosely a stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A clampdown is a firm move to stop an activity, a crackdown that puts an end to it.

clue.text: Black market transaction stopped by bishop

indicators.note: stopped by means plugged, so the clergy letter goes inside the deal

parts.note: a sale is a market transaction
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A black market deal halted by a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black market' reads as one phrase, but Black is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is black in heraldry and poetry, from the dark fur of the sable.

clue.text: Call to support penniless agent's activity

indicators.note: in a down clue the support goes below, so the phone word follows

parts.note: broke means having no money
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A phone call to help an agent who has no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Brokering is arranging deals between parties, which is what a broker or agent does.

clue.text: Antisocial behaviour of warrior or regularly seizing goods

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the regular letters go round the goods
regularly takes every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: G stands for good, so goods gives two of them

explanation.surface: A soldier's bad conduct, or habitually grabbing property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes ARO from warrior, which takes in GG; 'of' and 'or' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive, troublesome behaviour, especially by youths.

clue.text: Not heeding more than fifty plugs right under one's nose

indicators.note: plugs means fills a hole, so the number goes inside the plain-to-see word

parts.note: something right under one's nose is obvious, plain to see
LI is 51 in Roman numerals, one more than fifty

explanation.surface: Not noticing more than fifty adverts that are plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugs' looks like advertising but signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone oblivious is unaware of what is going on, not paying attention.

clue.text: Physical unit formerly found in dictionary

indicators.note: found in places the old word inside the reference book's letters

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
erst is an archaic word for formerly

explanation.surface: An old measurement located in a reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: The oersted is the CGS unit of magnetic field strength, named after Hans Christian Oersted.

clue.text: Vocal works principal violinist heard

indicators.note: heard means listened to, so the word for the orchestra's chief violinist is taken by its sound

parts.note: the leader of an orchestra is its principal first violinist in British usage

explanation.surface: Songs the first violin listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs for voice and piano, such as those of Schubert.

clue.text: Enthralling work first seen in Prado by mature artist

indicators.note: first seen in gives the opening letter of the museum's name

parts.note: to age is to mature
J M W Turner was the English painter

explanation.surface: A gripping painting first seen in Madrid's museum by an older painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A page-turner is a book so gripping that the reader cannot stop.

clue.text: In an Indian state, openings for united dairies' cheese

indicators.note: in places the two openings inside the state's name

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast

indicators.note: openings for takes the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: In an Indian state, new outlets for a dairy cooperative's cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a mild yellow Dutch cheese named after a town in Holland.

clue.text: Country without any source of infection?

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the little word is removed from the country

parts.note: Germany is a country

explanation.surface: A nation with no disease at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is a microbe that causes disease, the source of an infection.

clue.text: Short New Zealander accepts new patch

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the shortened native takes in the letter for new
short means cut off at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a Maori is a native New Zealander

explanation.surface: A small New Zealander takes on new territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the I of MAORI to leave MAOR, around N. Manor is British slang for a police officer's or gang's home territory.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, a manor is someone's home territory or beat, their patch.

clue.text: Piece of furniture incomplete until now

indicators.note: incomplete means not finished, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: so far means until now

explanation.surface: An item for the home still not finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an upholstered seat for several people, a piece of furniture.

clue.text: After ceaseless work man has first of trucks loaded

indicators.note: after places the man and truck letters behind the cut work
ceaseless means without an end, so the last letter of the work goes

parts.note: opus is Latin for a work, especially of music
Len is a man's name, short for Leonard

indicators.note: first of gives the opening letter of trucks

explanation.surface: After nonstop labour a man has his lorries filled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ceaseless' turns OPUS into OPU; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent and loaded are both ways of saying very wealthy.

clue.text: Feeling poorly, omit one

indicators.note: poorly means badly, a sign that the seven letters are to be put in another order

explanation.surface: Feeling unwell, leave someone out.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a feeling such as joy, anger or grief.

clue.text: Abandoned in Red Sea, it's left in UK

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and uninhibited, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Left stranded in the Red Sea, it is a British road term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' reads as marooned, but it means unrestrained here; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, where traffic keeps left, the nearside of a vehicle is the side nearer the kerb, its left.

clue.text: Harry right behind Mark?

indicators.note: behind puts the letter after the emblem

parts.note: a badge is a mark or emblem of identity

explanation.surface: Prince Harry standing just to the right of a man called Mark?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' and 'Mark' read as names, but harry is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger and to harry both mean to pester someone persistently.
